questionText:
At the time of death of a partner, undistributed Losses appearing in the
balance sheet of the old firm is transferred to
the capital account of:

options.text: Old partners in the gaining ratio
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.

options.text: Deceased partner only
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.

options.text: Continuing partners in the new profit sharing ratio
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

options.text: Old partners in old profit sharing ratio
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately identifies the verified NCERT concept for Realisation Account.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
According to NCERT principles for Dissolution of Partnership Firm (Realisation Account):
Old partners in old profit sharing ratio

Detailed Context:
1. Pre-existing losses appearing on the asset side of the balance sheet belong to the firm before death occurred.
2. The deceased partner was a co-owner during the period these losses accumulated.
3. Therefore, all old partners bear their respective shares:
   Old Partners' Capital A/cs Dr. (in old profit-sharing ratio)
   To Profit and Loss Account.

Therefore, option (D) is the correct answer.

questionText: [Set 46.17] According to Section 48 of the Indian Partnership Act, 1932, upon dissolution of a firm, assets including any sums contributed by partners shall be applied first in paying:

options.text: Debts of the firm to third parties (outside liabilities)
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately solves the problem for Settlement of Accounts on Dissolution.

options.text: Advances and loans made by partners to the firm
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.

options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.

options.text: Surplus distributed among partners in profit ratio
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
For Settlement of Accounts on Dissolution (Dissolution of Partnership Firm):
Detailed Solution:
According to NCERT Class 12 Accountancy (Dissolution of a Partnership Firm - Settlement of Accounts on Dissolution):
Order of settlement of accounts under Section 48: (1) In paying the debts of the firm to third parties (outside creditors), (2) In paying rateably to each partner loans/advances beyond capital, (3) In paying to each partner rateably what is due on account of capital, (4) Residue divided among partners in profit sharing ratio.

Hence, Option (D) is the correct answer.

Therefore, option (A) is the correct answer.

questionText:
Match List-I with List-II
 
List-I (Different accounts)
List-II (Related transaction)
(A) Profit and Loss Account
(I) Dissolution of Partnership
(B) Profit and Loss Appropriation Account (II) Dissolution of Firm
(C) Revaluation Account
(III) Interest on Loan to Partner
(D) Realization Account
(IV) Transfer to Reserve
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.
Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.
Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.
Correct answer. Correctly maps each entity across columns.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
1. (A) Profit and Loss Account: Records charges against profit, including Interest on Loan to Partner -> (III).
2. (B) Profit and Loss Appropriation Account: Records distributions of profit, such as Transfer to Reserve -> (IV).
3. (C) Revaluation Account: Prepared on reconstitution (Dissolution of Partnership) -> (I).
4. (D) Realization Account: Prepared on closure of entity (Dissolution of Firm) -> (II).
5. Correct matching: (A)-(III), (B)-(IV), (C)-(I), (D)-(II).
Hence, option (D) is the correct match.

questionText: [Set 41.50] According to Section 48 of the Indian Partnership Act, 1932, upon dissolution of a firm, assets including any sums contributed by partners shall be applied first in paying:

options.text: Advances and loans made by partners to the firm
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.

options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately solves the problem for Settlement of Accounts on Dissolution.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
For Settlement of Accounts on Dissolution (Dissolution of Partnership Firm):
Detailed Solution:
According to NCERT Class 12 Accountancy (Dissolution of a Partnership Firm - Settlement of Accounts on Dissolution):
Order of settlement of accounts under Section 48: (1) In paying the debts of the firm to third parties (outside creditors), (2) In paying rateably to each partner loans/advances beyond capital, (3) In paying to each partner rateably what is due on account of capital, (4) Residue divided among partners in profit sharing ratio.

Hence, Option (C) is the correct answer.

Therefore, option (B) is the correct answer.
